streetwear.prompt:
User brief: An owl with one raised wing.
Create one finished original logo, with crisp edges and purposeful optical spacing. Follow any background specified in the brief; otherwise use a plain #191919 background. The canvas is square; keep the entire mark, lettering and extended details inside the artboard with comfortable clear space. No mockup or presentation grid.
Selected style: streetwear-lettering. Create a custom typographic illustration for apparel: the letterforms themselves are the artwork. The selected Lettering style determines the actual glyph anatomy, joins, proportions and terminals. Construct that genre first, before adding color, outlines or depth. Preserve its characteristic counters and spacing rather than forcing every genre into narrow ornamental letters. The selected Lettering style is authoritative over shared art direction and concept suggestions. Streetwear is the application, not a Gothic font requirement. Gothic stems, chisel notches, swashes, connecting strokes and exaggerated outer letters belong only to genres that call for them. Do not carry these features between unrelated styles. Give the main name visual dominance; supporting text, when supplied, is much smaller. Use crisp drawn ink regions and hard boundaries. When depth is selected, construct broad light and dark face planes, stepped shadow bands and one consistent offset direction. Keep the construction visible across the letters, not just in a thin rim. Flat treatment removes all shading while retaining the custom letter structure. Avoid soft airbrushed gradients, photographic material lighting and glossy mockup effects. Keep a compact, front-facing lockup with all letter terminals, swashes and depth inside the artboard. Show one finished mark on a uniform background, without texture, vignette, floor or mockup. Invent no captions, dates, slogans, signatures or contact details. Add symbols or decorative objects only when the user requests them; keep every requested letter readable.
Preserve the user brief’s subjects, essential motifs, object relationships and explicit visual preferences. Style defaults and optional construction never replace an explicit instruction.
The exact brand name is "DARKMEN". Spell every letter exactly; apply any explicitly selected case, otherwise preserve the supplied case.
Do not invent a tagline.
Preserve the exact brand spelling and case unless explicitly asked to change case. Lettering is the dominant artwork; integrate requested motifs without obscuring the letters.
Follow colors specified in the brief and controls; choose a restrained palette only where colors are unspecified.
Automatic ink palette: follow explicit color preferences in the brief; otherwise use silver-white letter faces, two clearly separated gray shade regions and a restrained teal separation keyline, with a dark separating base where contrast needs it. For Flat, use uniform silver-white faces and the keyline only; no shade regions. Keep all regions crisp.
Style default, only where the brief and controls leave a choice unspecified: Auto layout: follow any explicit layout preference in the brief; otherwise use a sculpted arched word envelope for a short name, adjusting letter heights and extending the outer letters. For several words use tightly balanced rows when needed. Preserve reading order and never split a single word into invented words.
Style default, only where the brief and controls leave a choice unspecified: Auto outline: follow any explicit outline preference in the brief; otherwise use layered separation outlines with a dark base, controlled accent keylines and open counters. Keep the outer keyline fine; avoid repeated thick concentric borders.
Style default, only where the brief and controls leave a choice unspecified: Auto depth: follow any explicit finish preference in the brief; otherwise draw broad chiseled bevel planes, crisp inset highlights, stepped shade bands and consistent offset side depth. Use hard-edged ink regions, not soft photographic lighting.
Required design control (overrides conflicting brief text and style defaults): Lettering style: Gothic. Draw tall condensed ornamental Gothic/blackletter-inspired display letters with waisted vertical stems, narrow open counters, sharp inset cuts and flared wedge terminals. Coordinate oversized first and last letters with the inner letters into a dense, sculpted word silhouette. Preserve every requested letter and its case; avoid a stock medieval font with a decorative border. Required glyph anatomy (takes priority over shared styling): Use upright broken blackletter strokes; exclude connected brush script, sports slabs and tribal branches. Outlines and bevels must follow these glyphs, never replace their construction.
Resolve all design decisions into one coherent mark. For flat treatments use uniformly colored regions with hard boundaries. Preserve detail only when the chosen style calls for it.
